claims.statement: Google Ads treats a primary conversion action as biddable only when a campaign uses the goal containing that action. Secondary actions are observation-only except that a secondary action included in a custom goal is used for bidding when that custom goal is selected. Enhanced conversions supplement existing measurement with hashed first-party data subject to applicable policy and consent requirements.
claims.scope: Google Ads standard-goal and custom-goal bidding controls; feature eligibility and diagnostics remain account-specific

claims.statement: Meta Conversions API connects website, app, business messaging, and offline event data to Meta and can operate alongside Meta Pixel and other connection channels. Verify receipt, matching, and deduplication in current setup diagnostics; consent remains implementation-specific.
claims.scope: Meta runtime measurement controls; no universal performance lift or EMQ threshold is asserted
claims.notes: 2026-10-07: Exact substantive public official documentation independently verified in a normal browser render after text retrieval failed. 2026-10-12: Pixel redundancy and deduplication wording verified on the deduplication page. This establishes documentation support only, not an authenticated account request or account health.

claims.statement: TikTok supports website measurement through Pixel, Events API, or both, and recommends deduplication when Pixel and Events API send the same business event.

claims.statement: Microsoft Advertising uses UET for website conversion tracking, offers a documented server-side Conversions API with a public endpoint, payload schema, partner integrations, and UET deduplication through a shared event ID, and documents Google Ads import mappings and limitations requiring post-import validation. claims.statement: Google's consent-mode pages word the modeling click threshold differently. The modeling page gives a daily threshold of 700 ad clicks over a seven-day period per country and domain grouping, and the verification page gives 700 ad clicks over 7 days for a domain and country grouping without the word daily. A third page lists 100 clicks per day per country and domain grouping for basic consent mode only. Google does not reconcile these figures, so they stay unreconciled. The separate impact-results page says additional volume and modeling thresholds apply without publishing another numeric click threshold. The active setup and current diagnostics remain controlling evidence.
claims.scope: Google consent-mode modeling eligibility and impact-results surfaces; wording varies by page and no unpublished threshold is inferred

claims.scope: EU AI Act Article 50; final applicability remains fact-specific

claims.statement: In a Google Ads account, when several keywords targeting the same domain are eligible for the same search term they do not compete with each other in the auction and only one of them triggers an ad. Exact match keywords identical to the term are prioritized first, then phrase and broad match keywords or search themes identical to the term; among equal-priority candidates the ad with the highest Ad Rank is chosen. A keyword in a budget-restricted campaign will not always be able to trigger an ad even when it otherwise could.
claims.scope: Google Ads in-account keyword, DSA, and search-theme selection; auction outcomes and account-specific costs remain unobserved

claims.statement: Dynamic Search Ads are ranked the same way as keyword-based ads. When a person searches for the exact keyword targeted in another campaign of the same account or a linked account, the keyword campaign's ad may show instead of the Dynamic Search Ad; the Dynamic Search Ad may show instead when the search term is a broad or phrase match to a keyword and the Dynamic Search Ad has the higher Ad Rank. DSA ad groups without keywords are selected on highest Ad Rank compared with other ads in the account.
claims.scope: Google Ads in-account keyword, DSA, and search-theme selection; auction outcomes and account-specific costs remain unobserved

claims.statement: Dynamic Search Ads targeting matches searches to pages on the advertiser's site through dynamic ad targets, whose options include an all-webpages target covering every crawled page on the domain as well as narrower URL, page feed, title, content, and category targets.

Since October 1, 2026 SALES and LEAD_GENERATION are supported for Max campaigns. Report limits announced for December 8 (HOUR breakdowns beyond seven days or unsupported breakdown combinations) remain scheduled on October 12.

claims.statement: Meta released Graph API and Marketing API v26.0 on 2026-07-29. The Marketing API v24.0 expiry date that Meta lists (2026-10-06) has passed. From v26.0, creating Housing, Employment, or Financial Products and Services ad sets with relaxable targeting in a non-broad setup requires targeting_automation.advantage_audience to be set explicitly; Meta's launch post limits this to creation, and earlier versions follow only after v25.0 is deprecated.
